criteria.A: Isolated staging area plus pointer flip: target state is assembled and checked in staging tables invisible to normal reads, and one fenced write both publishes the rows and records the new installed snapshot.
criteria.B: In-table dual versions plus pointer flip: every migrated row exists in installed and staged variants in the same tables distinguished by snapshot id, live traffic sees only installed variants until the pointer moves.
criteria.C: Full dataset copy plus alias flip: the migration copies each row into a new namespace, the copy is validated as a whole, and activation switches per-model aliases to the new namespace under the fence.

approach.instructions: The engine team can implement only one migration execution approach now. Weighing resumability, the single-fenced-commit activation rule, protection of installed data during staging, and honest row-version and history semantics, which approach is the strongest choice?
